title: Theory of High-Temperature Fractional Chern Phases in Monolayer van der Waals Kagome Materials A$_2$T$_3$X$_4$
authors: Soomin Oh, Jiyong Han, Jinhyeok Choi, Donghae Seo, Mingu Kang, Gil Young Cho
abstract: Fractional Chern insulators bring the fractional quantum Hall effect, with its anyonic excitations, to zero magnetic field. So far they have been realized in moiré materials, where the long superlattice period weakens electronic interactions and confines these phases to cryogenic temperatures. Early proposals instead envisioned topological flat bands on atomic-scale lattices, where fractionalization could persist to far higher temperatures, but a suitable material has been lacking. Here we theoretically identify monolayers of the recently synthesized van der Waals kagome family $\mathrm{A}_2\mathrm{T}_3\mathrm{X}_4$ as such a platform, combining intrinsic topological flat bands and strong Coulomb interactions with gate-tunable carrier density and layer assembly. Exact diagonalization of models derived from density functional theory reveals ferromagnetism over broad filling ranges, supporting diverse fractional Chern insulators, anomalous composite Fermi liquids, and charge-ordered phases. In particular, in $\mathrm{Cs}_2\mathrm{Pd}_3\mathrm{S}_4$, the fractional Chern insulator exhibits a many-body gap of approximately 26 meV in the largest system accessible with band mixing allowing at most one interband electron-hole excitation. Layer assembly further provides a natural route to fractional quantum spin Hall insulators: bilayers with antiparallel magnetizations support this phase at realistic separations. These results identify an experimentally accessible material family in which chemical composition, carrier density, and stacking offer complementary routes to fractionalization at enhanced energy scales and control over topological order.
summary: This theoretical study identifies van der Waals kagome materials as a promising platform for realizing high-temperature Fractional Chern Insulators. By combining intrinsic topological flat bands with strong Coulomb interactions, the authors predict multiple correlated phases, including FCIs and anomalous composite Fermi liquids. The work details computational methods using DFT and exact diagonalization to map out the phase space based on chemical tuning and carrier density.
main_problem: The paper aims to theoretically identify and study a material platform capable of realizing high-temperature Fractional Chern Insulators (FCIs) and other correlated topological phases, overcoming the limitations of current cryogenic moiré materials.
main_result: The van der Waals kagome material family A2T3X4 is proposed as a viable platform, exhibiting intrinsic topological flat bands and strong interactions that support diverse correlated states like FCIs and anomalous composite Fermi liquids at enhanced energy scales.
method: The study employs Density Functional Theory (DFT) to derive parameters for a tight-binding model, followed by Exact Diagonalization (ED) to investigate electron-electron correlations and spontaneous symmetry breaking.
model_or_system: The system is the monolayer van der Waals kagome material A2T3X4. The model incorporates a tight-binding Hamiltonian with hopping and spin-orbit coupling, and electron-electron interactions are treated via an Ohno interaction potential.
key_observables: Chern numbers, many-body gaps (e.g., $\approx 26 	ext{ meV}$), structure factors $S(q)$, and momentum occupation number $n(k)$ are used to diagnose various correlated phases.
important_parameters:
Gate-tunable carrier density, chemical composition (A, T, X sites), and layer stacking distance ($d/a$) are key tuning parameters. Fillings $
u_{	ext{tot}}$ are varied across several fractional values.
main_assumptions: The analysis often projects onto the two spin components of the uppermost kagome band, treating lower bands as inert, and uses the Ohno interaction as a phenomenological description of interactions.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate phase diagrams showing different correlated states, band structures comparing DFT and tight-binding fits, and detailed spectral/structure factor analysis for specific phases like ACFLs and CDWs.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by first establishing the theoretical framework using DFT and tight-binding models, then applying ED to map out phase diagrams for various fillings, and finally detailing the signatures of specific phases (FCI, ACFL, CDW) using advanced diagnostics.
why_interesting: The work provides a concrete, chemically tunable material family ($	ext{A}_2	ext{T}_3	ext{X}_4$) for realizing exotic topological states at higher temperatures, which is highly relevant for condensed matter theorists studying strongly correlated electron systems.

FIG. 3: Exact Diagonalization of Cs2Pd3S4. (a) Many-body spectra at νtot = 4/3 of system size N = 24. (b) Spectral flow under flux insertion at νtot = 4/3 of system size N = 18. (c) Many-body spectra at νtot = 3/2 of system size N = 24.
